assignment.title: Algebra I — DOL #4 Makeup
assignment.instructions: This is the makeup for District DOL #4. Its 13 questions test the same skills as the 13 questions on the DOL, in the same order, with new numbers and new situations. Show your work inside each tool. You have 3 tries on each question, and hints are there when you need them.

questions.prompt: The table shows some ordered pairs of linear function f. Use three different pairs of rows to find the rate of change of f and show that it is constant. Then find the y-intercept and write the function in slope-intercept form, y = mx + b.
hints: For each pair of rows, Δx is the change in x and Δy is the change in y. The rate of change is Δy ÷ Δx.
The x-values do not go up by 1, so the rate of change is not just the change in y from one row to the next.
The y-intercept is the value of b. Substitute your slope and the x- and y-values from one row into y = mx + b, then solve for b.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The rate of change between two rows of a table is…
options: the change in x divided by the change in y
the change in y divided by the change in x
scaffold.correct: the change in y divided by the change in x

solutionReview.commonError: Using the change in y alone as the rate of change; from x = −6 to x = −2 the x-values go up by 4, so the rate is Δy ÷ Δx = 10 ÷ 4 = 5/2, and then b = −8 − (5/2)(−2) = −3.

questions.prompt: What value of n makes the equation (3/5)(n − 10) = (2/5)(n − 20) true? Solve it step by step.
hints: Both sides have a denominator of 5. Multiply both sides by 5 to clear the fractions first.
After you clear the fractions, distribute on each side.
Collect the n-terms on one side and the constants on the other, then check your value in the ORIGINAL equation.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Multiplying both sides of (3/5)(n − 10) = (2/5)(n − 20) by 5 gives…

reasoning: Subtract 2n from both sides: n − 30 = −40. Add 30 to both sides: n = −10.
Check: (3/5)(−20) = −12 and (2/5)(−30) = −12, so both sides are equal.
solutionReview.commonError: Distributing the fraction to only the first term in the parentheses, for example writing (3/5)(n − 10) as (3/5)n − 10.

questions.prompt: A club is selling candy bars for a fundraiser. The graph shows the number of candy bars the club still has to sell, y, after x days of selling, from the first day until the candy bars are gone. Determine the reasonable domain and range for this situation. Write each one as an inequality.

graph.accessibleDescription: A line segment that falls from left to right. It starts at a closed dot on the vertical axis and ends at a closed dot on the horizontal axis. The horizontal axis is time selling in days, marked every day. The vertical axis is candy bars left to sell, marked every 30 candy bars.

hints: The domain is the set of x-values the graph covers: the days, read from the left end of the graph to the right end.
The range is the set of y-values the graph covers: the candy bars left, read from the lowest point of the graph to the highest point.
Both ends of the graph are closed dots, so both endpoint values belong in the inequality. Use ≤, not <.

solutionReview.commonError: Swapping the domain and the range; the range is about y, the candy bars left, so it runs from 0 to 360, not from 0 to 12.

questions.prompt: Graph the line that has a slope of 3/4 and a y-intercept of −2. Start at the y-intercept, then use the slope to find a second point.
hints: The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis, where x = 0. Plot that point first.
A slope of 3/4 means a rise of 3 for every run of 4 to the right.
From the y-intercept, go up 3 and right 4 to plot your second point, then draw the line through both points.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. A slope of 3/4 tells you to move from one point on the line to the next by going…

solutionReview.commonError: Reading 3/4 as rise 4 and run 3; the top of the slope is the rise, so from (0, −2) the line goes up 3 and right 4 to (4, 1).

questions.prompt: The graph shows the function f(x) = x. It was transformed to create the graph of the function g(x) = f(x) + 5. Describe how the graphs of the functions f and g are related.

graph.accessibleDescription: The graph of the parent function f(x) = x: a line that rises from left to right through the origin on a grid marked every unit from −10 to 10 on both axes.

responses.label: Which way is the graph of g moved from the graph of f?
How many units is it moved?
The y-intercept of the graph of f
The y-intercept of the graph of g
The y-intercept of the graph of g is…
options: 5 units greater than the y-intercept of the graph of f
5 units less than the y-intercept of the graph of f
the same as the y-intercept of the graph of f
5 times the y-intercept of the graph of f
responses.answer: 5 units greater than the y-intercept of the graph of f

hints: The number in g(x) = f(x) + 5 is added outside f(x), so it changes the outputs, the y-values. That is a vertical move.
Adding a positive number to every output moves every point of the graph higher by that many units.
A y-intercept is where a graph crosses the y-axis. Find where the graph of f crosses it, then move that point the way the rule for g moves every point.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. In g(x) = f(x) + 5, the 5 is added to…

reasoning: The 5 is added outside f(x), so every output goes up by 5: the graph of g is the graph of f translated up 5 units.
f(x) = x crosses the y-axis at 0, so the y-intercept of f is 0.
g(0) = f(0) + 5 = 0 + 5 = 5, so the y-intercept of g is 5, which is 5 units greater than the y-intercept of f.
solutionReview.commonError: Moving the graph right 5 units; a number added outside f(x) changes the y-values, so the move is vertical: up 5.

questions.prompt: What is the value of w that makes the equation 4(w + 3) = 3(w − 5) true? Solve it step by step.
hints: Distribute on each side first: multiply the number outside the parentheses by BOTH terms inside.
Subtract 3w from both sides so the w-terms are on one side.
Undo the constant on the w side, then check your value in the ORIGINAL equation.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Distributing on the right side, 3(w − 5) becomes…

solutionReview.commonError: Adding 12 instead of subtracting it at the last step, which gives w = −3; to undo + 12, subtract 12 from both sides.

questions.prompt: A student is paying for a used bike. The table shows the remaining balance in dollars, y, after the student has made x equal payments. Identify the domain and the range of the function for this situation.

responses.label: The number of payments can be…

hints: The domain is the set of x-values: the numbers of payments the student can make.
A student cannot make half a payment, so list only the whole numbers in the table's x column.
The range is the set of y-values, the balances in the table. Write each set with braces, like {1, 2, 3}.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The domain of this function is made of…

reasoning: x counts payments, and a student makes whole payments only, so the domain is the x-values in the table.
The range is the balances that go with those payments: {0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150}.
solutionReview.commonError: Giving the balances as the domain; the domain is the inputs, the number of payments, so it is {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

questions.prompt: A sequence can be generated using the rule aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + 1.7, where a₁ = 6.5 is the first term of the sequence. Use the recursive rule to find the first 4 terms, plot them, and identify the common difference.
hints: A recursive rule tells you how to get each term from the term just before it.
Start with the first term, a₁. Apply the rule to it to get a₂, then apply the rule again to a₂ to get a₃.
Plot each term as the point (n, aₙ). Do not connect the points: n is a whole-number term position.

solutionReview.commonError: Multiplying by 1.7 instead of adding it; the rule adds 1.7 to the term before, so the terms are 6.5, 8.2, 9.9, 11.6.

questions.prompt: The graph of a linear function passes through the two marked points, (−6, 1) and (6, 4). Find the slope, then write the equation of the line in point-slope form and in slope-intercept form.
hints: Use the slope formula with the two marked points: (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). Subtract in the same order on the top and the bottom.
Point-slope form is y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Use your slope and either marked point.
Solve your point-slope equation for y to get slope-intercept form.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. In y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), the values x₁ and y₁ come from…

solutionReview.commonError: Writing the point-slope form with the wrong signs, such as y − 1 = (1/4)(x − 6) for the point (−6, 1); subtracting −6 makes x + 6, so it is y − 1 = (1/4)(x + 6).

questions.prompt: The graph of a linear function is shown on the grid. Find the x-intercept and the y-intercept of the function.

graph.accessibleDescription: A line that rises from left to right on a coordinate grid marked every unit from −6 to 6 on both axes. It crosses the vertical axis below the origin and the horizontal axis to the right of the origin.

hints: The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis, the vertical axis. There, x = 0.
The x-intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis, the horizontal axis. There, y = 0.
Count the grid lines from the origin carefully. Each grid line is 1 unit.

misconceptions.message: That is where the line crosses the x-axis. The y-intercept is where it crosses the y-axis, the vertical axis.

solutionReview.commonError: Mixing up the intercepts; the line crosses the vertical y-axis at −2 and the horizontal x-axis at 5.

questions.prompt: What value of z makes the equation (3/2)z + 8 = −2((1/4)z + 6) true? Solve it step by step.
hints: Distribute −2 on the right side to BOTH terms inside the parentheses. Watch the signs.
Add (1/2)z to both sides so the z-terms are on the left.
Subtract 8 from both sides, then divide by the coefficient of z. Check your value in the ORIGINAL equation.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Distributing on the right side, −2((1/4)z + 6) becomes…

reasoning: Subtract 8 from both sides: 2z = −20. Divide by 2: z = −10.
solutionReview.commonError: Multiplying −2 by only the first term, which gives −(1/2)z + 6; the −2 multiplies the 6 too, so the right side is −(1/2)z − 12.

questions.prompt: Read the moving-van situation. Find the cost per mile and the flat fee, then write the linear equation for the total cost in dollars, y, for renting a van and driving it x miles.

source.prompt: A moving-van company charges a flat fee to rent a van and a cost per mile for driving it. One customer rented a van and drove it 30 miles for a total cost of $64. Another customer rented a van and drove it 120 miles for a total cost of $118. Let x be the number of miles driven and y be the total cost, in dollars.

slopeMeaning.value: The total cost goes up $0.60 for each mile driven.
choices: The total cost goes up $0.60 for each mile driven.
The total cost goes up $46 for each mile driven.

yInterceptMeaning.value: The customer pays a $46 flat fee before driving any miles.
choices: The customer pays a $46 flat fee before driving any miles.
The customer pays $64 before driving any miles.
The van can be driven 46 miles.

hints: The two customers give two points, (30, 64) and (120, 118). The cost per mile is the slope: change in cost ÷ change in miles.
The flat fee is the cost when x = 0, so it is the y-intercept. Substitute the slope and one customer's point into y = mx + b and solve for b.
Write y = mx + b with your slope and y-intercept.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The cost per mile is found by dividing…
options: the change in total cost by the change in miles
one customer's total cost by that customer's miles
scaffold.correct: the change in total cost by the change in miles

solutionReview.commonError: Dividing one customer's cost by the miles, such as 64 ÷ 30; that includes the flat fee. Use the change: (118 − 64) ÷ (120 − 30) = 54 ÷ 90 = 0.6 dollars per mile, and then 64 = 0.6(30) + b gives b = 46.

questions.prompt: A store held an online sale. The data show the number of customers, y, during each hour, x hours after the sale began. First estimate a line of best fit by moving the slope and the intercept yourself. Then run linear regression to write a linear function that best models the data. Use the regression function to predict the number of customers 8 hours after the sale began.
hints: The number of customers falls each hour, so your line should fall from left to right. Slide it until about as many points sit above it as below it.
Run linear regression on all seven data points. Its line replaces your estimate as your model.
Substitute 8 for x in the regression function y = mx + b, then round to the nearest whole customer.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. To predict the number of customers 8 hours after the sale began, you substitute 8 for…
options: x, the hours after the sale began
scaffold.correct: x, the hours after the sale began

solutionReview.commonError: Writing the model from the first two rows only, or using the first row's value as the y-intercept; the y-intercept is the value at x = 0, and the best model comes from linear regression on all seven points.
